title: Change management: why a department resists the number

videos.script: For six years, Sandra's team was told it was doing well. Deliveries on time, ninety-four percent, green on every dashboard. {{green}} Then an analyst arrives with a different number, eighty-two point seven, and the same team is suddenly the cause of a problem. {{different}} Nobody in that team will say they resist the number. They will ask about the definition, the months, the method. Every question reasonable. Together, a wall. {{wall}} Resistance is not stupidity, and it is rarely about the data. It is about what the number says about people, their work and their standing. {{about}} This lesson looks at why the wall goes up, two models for taking it down, and what Faro did. And it follows the pilot to the end, because a change is not made in the meeting that approves it. {{end}}
